newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria still negotiating wheat purchases - trader.
newsitem.headline: Algeria still negotiating wheat purchases - trader.

text.p: Algeria is still negotiating the purchase of 75,000 tonnes of soft wheat and 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat, European grain traders said on Monday.
"They are still working on it," one trader said, adding results were expected later in the week.
"They have not bought anything yet," another trader said.
Exporters made offers to sell late on Friday but further details were not available.

Last week Algeria tendered for 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat for September shipment and for 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in August and September from the United States, Canada or Syria.

A severe drought could cut Algeria's grain harvest to a 20-year low of about 1.05 million tonnes in the 1996/97 season from a record 4.9 million the previous season, the official Algerian news agency APS has said.
